output.summary: Attrition is 14.1% against a firm five-year average of 15.0% and a regional median of 18.0%, so there is no retention crisis. Two September resignations that drew attention were driven by pre-existing in-house and relocation plans (E5, E6), not the Friday change. Complaints are real but concentrated on Fridays, a tradeoff the Executive Committee knowingly accepted (E7). Intent to stay is flat (73% to 71%), and flexibility satisfaction fell (3.9 to 3.1). Whether the junior skill gaps have closed is unproven, since Q3 mentoring satisfaction and logged sessions are confounded by new curriculum and logging changes. Best action is to report the facts, keep the existing review triggers, and communicate the rationale. A blanket bonus is unjustified, and identifying the associates in the kitchen conversation would be harmful.
